title: Cauchy-Schwarz on the constructed plane, in its UNSQUARED form
statement: For plane vectors U and V, <U,V> <= sqrt(<U,U> * <V,V>). `CPoint.cauchy_schwarz` states the squared form <U,V>^2 <= <U,U><V,V>, which is what Lagrange's identity plus positive semidefiniteness deliver; carrying it under `CReal.sqrt_le_sqrt` leaves sqrt(t*t) on the left, and recovering t from that is the whole difficulty. `CReal.sqrt_sq` will not do it: it requires 0 <= t, and the cross term <U,V> has no known sign -- at U = (1,0), V = (-1,0) it is -1. Nor is a case split available: CReal has no le_or_lt, and the converse of `not_equiv_of_apart` is Markov's principle, which this development neither proves nor assumes. What closes it is `CReal.mul_self_abs` (|t|*|t| ~ t*t, UNCONDITIONAL) composed with sqrt_sq at |t|, then `CReal.le_abs_self`. That is the same obstruction and the same resolution `Complex.abs_add_le` needed, recorded at length in ComplexPrelude::norm_sq_add_le's doc comment along with the routes that were tried and refuted.

formal.statement: theorem Metric.CPoint.dotLeSqrtMul : ((x0 : CPoint) -> ((x1 : CPoint) -> CReal.le (CPoint.dot x0 x1) (CReal.sqrt (CReal.mul (CPoint.dot x0 x0) (CPoint.dot x1 x1)))))

evidence.supports: Metric.CPoint.dotLeSqrtMul is admitted by the trusted kernel gate with the type recorded in formal.statement, and Kernel::axiom_footprint reports 0 assumed names.
checkers: producing-build (Kernel::add_declaration, which re-derives the type from the proof term)
evidence.checker_command: cargo run -q --release -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example kernel_declaration_projection -- --require-declaration Metric.CPoint.dotLeSqrtMul | grep -cE '^found[[:space:]]+metric[[:space:]]+theorem[[:space:]]+Metric\.CPoint\.dotLeSqrtMul[[:space:]]+0$'
evidence.notes: The exit status depends on the finding twice over. kernel_declaration_projection exits NON-ZERO and prints an explanatory error when the named declaration is in no constructed prelude's environment -- asking for a declaration and finding none is a failure there, not an empty answer. grep -c then exits 1 printing 0 if the anchored row is absent or its axiom-footprint column is not 0. Anchored with [[:space:]], never \t: in a scripted (GNU) grep \t is a literal t, and 68 fact checkers in this ledger were wrong for exactly that reason. grep -c rather than grep -q, which would SIGPIPE the producer under pipefail. --release is MANDATORY: this binary builds creal/complex/cpoint/metric, which overflow the default debug thread stack. The `metric` label did not exist in this tool before the commit of record; without it the tool was blind to the prelude, which is indistinguishable from the declaration not existing.

provenance.source: Lane `topology-decision`, roadmap W0-3 and W2-1, decided in ADR-1602 (docs/research/09-decisions/adr-1602-the-metric-layer-first-then-pointfree-and-not-open-sets.md). formal.statement is Kernel::render_lean of the declaration's type, taken verbatim from the unfiltered emit of `kernel_declaration_projection`; axiom_footprint is that tool's footprint-size column, which reads Kernel::axiom_footprint.

notes: WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED. This is the ONE-SIDED bound <U,V> <= sqrt(<U,U><V,V>), not the two-sided |<U,V>| <= ||U||*||V||. The two-sided form is reachable by the same route (the proof already passes through |<U,V>| <= sqrt(<U,U><V,V>) as an intermediate step) but was not declared, because the triangle inequality needs only the one-sided direction and an undeclared step is not a theorem. Anyone who wants the norm form should lift that intermediate step rather than assume it exists.
